### `MlxArray`

```rust
pub struct MlxArray
```

Owned MLX array handle released exactly once through the official C API.

### `MlxArray::from_f32`

```rust
pub fn from_f32(values: &[f32], shape: &[i32]) -> Result<Self, MlxCError>
```

Creates a float32 array from host values laid out in row-major order. The values are copied, so later changes to the slice do not affect the array.

**Errors:** Fails when the shape's element count differs from the value count.

**Errors:** Fails when the shape's element count differs from the value count.

### `MlxArray::empty`


Creates an empty handle holding no array, for passing as an output parameter. Evaluating it or reading its values returns an error.

### `MlxArray::is_empty`

```rust

```

Whether this handle holds no array at all. A zero-sized array is a real array, so this reports `false` for it.

### `MlxArray::raw`

```rust
pub const fn raw(&self) -> raw::mlx_array
```

The underlying MLX-C handle, still owned by this value, for calling `raw` functions directly.

### `MlxArray::empty_raw`

```rust
pub const fn empty_raw() -> raw::mlx_array
```

The official absent-optional-handle placeholder for raw MLX calls.

Compiled-graph builders outside this crate mirror the runtime's own operations and need the same empty convention for absent `freqs`, `sinks`, and `global_scale` handles; the placeholder owns nothing and is always valid to pass by value.

### `MlxArray::raw_mut`

```rust
pub fn raw_mut(&mut self) -> *mut raw::mlx_array
```

A pointer to the underlying MLX-C handle, for `raw` functions that write their result through an output parameter.

### `MlxArray::require_populated`

```rust
pub fn require_populated(&self, operation: &'static str) -> Result<(), MlxCError>
```

Validates that a returned handle is populated, translating a parked payload-closure failure or the captured MLX-C description into a typed failure.

This is a pure translation: embedding-specific error classification (for example an active memory ceiling) is embedding policy and happens when the consumer converts this error at its boundary.

### `MlxArray::evaluate`

```rust
pub fn evaluate(&self) -> Result<(), MlxCError>
```

Materializes this lazy array and reports runtime failures without exit.

### `MlxArray::item_u32`

```rust
pub fn item_u32(&self) -> Result<u32, MlxCError>
```

Evaluates a scalar array and copies its value as an unsigned token ID.

**Errors:** Fails when the array is not a uint32 scalar. MLX validates the size but reinterprets rather than converts the element, so the type is checked here.

### `MlxArray::retain`

```rust
pub fn retain(&self) -> Result<Self, MlxCError>
```

Creates a shared reference to the same underlying MLX data.

MLX uses reference counting, so this is cheap and does not copy the tensor data. The returned array shares the same lazy graph and evaluated buffers as the source.

## `src/types/array_readback.rs`

Whole-array host reads: every path copying an array's elements into Rust memory, with the element type and storage layout checks they all share.

### `MlxArray::to_vec_f32`

```rust
pub fn to_vec_f32(&self) -> Result<Vec<f32>, MlxCError>
```

Evaluates the array and copies its float32 elements into Rust-owned memory in row-major order. Views such as transposes, reversals, and strided slices read in their logical order.

**Errors:** Fails when the array is not float32 or evaluation fails.

### `MlxArray::to_vec_u32`

```rust
pub fn to_vec_u32(&self) -> Result<Vec<u32>, MlxCError>
```

Evaluates the array and copies its uint32 elements into Rust-owned memory in row-major order.

**Errors:** Fails when the array is not uint32 or evaluation fails.

### `MlxArray::to_vec_u8`

```rust
pub fn to_vec_u8(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, MlxCError>
```

Evaluates the array and copies its uint8 elements into Rust-owned memory in row-major order.

**Errors:** Fails when the array is not uint8 or evaluation fails.

### `MlxArray::copy_evaluated_u8_values`

```rust
pub fn copy_evaluated_u8_values(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, MlxCError>
```

Copies a contiguous uint8 array in one host transfer.

Evaluate first so any wait is attributed to that call; an unevaluated array is evaluated here rather than read as absent storage.

**Errors:** Fails when the array is not uint8, or when its storage is a view: this method exists to attribute one direct transfer, so it never copies through a materialization the way `to_vec_u8` does.

### `MlxArray::copy_evaluated_u32_values`

```rust
pub fn copy_evaluated_u32_values(&self) -> Result<Vec<u32>, MlxCError>
```

Copies a contiguous uint32 array in one host transfer.

This split exists so performance attribution can distinguish the synchronization wait from the small host copy: evaluate first so any wait is attributed to that call; an unevaluated array is evaluated here rather than read as absent storage.

**Errors:** Fails when the array is not uint32, or when its storage is a view: this method never copies through a materialization the way `to_vec_u32` does.

### `MlxArray::to_vec_complex`

```rust
pub fn to_vec_complex(&self) -> Result<Vec<(f32, f32)>, MlxCError>
```

Evaluates the array and copies its complex elements, in row-major order, as `(real, imaginary)` pairs.

**Errors:** Fails when the array is not complex or evaluation fails.

### `MlxArray::is_row_contiguous`

```rust
pub fn is_row_contiguous(&self) -> Result<bool, MlxCError>
```

Whether this array's evaluated storage is one row-major contiguous run, which is what raw host reads require. Transposes, reversals, and strided slices are views over their parent's buffer and report `false`.

Evaluates the array first because MLX assigns storage flags only when the data materializes.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when evaluation or the query fails.

## `src/types/array_status.rs`

Array status queries: evaluation progress, storage layout, and printing.

### `MlxArray::is_available`

```rust
pub fn is_available(&self) -> Result<bool, MlxCError>
```

Whether the array's value is ready to read without waiting. Unlike the contiguity queries this never evaluates, so it can watch work started through `MlxBindingsContext::async_eval_arrays`.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when the query fails.

### `MlxArray::wait`

```rust
pub fn wait(&self) -> Result<(), MlxCError>
```

Blocks until this array's value is ready, scheduling it first if nothing has yet, after which `is_available` reports `true`.

This deliberately goes through evaluation rather than MLX-C's `_mlx_array_wait`: on an array nothing has scheduled, that call finds no event to wait on and marks the array available with no data behind it, leaving every later read of it or anything built on it a null buffer.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when evaluation fails.

### `MlxArray::is_contiguous`

```rust
pub fn is_contiguous(&self) -> Result<bool, MlxCError>
```

Whether the evaluated storage is one contiguous run in any axis order.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when evaluation or the query fails.

### `MlxArray::is_col_contiguous`

```rust
pub fn is_col_contiguous(&self) -> Result<bool, MlxCError>
```

Whether the evaluated storage is one column-major contiguous run.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when evaluation or the query fails.

### `MlxArray::to_string_lossy`

```rust
pub fn to_string_lossy(&self) -> Result<String, MlxCError>
```

Renders the array as MLX prints it, evaluating it first. Precision and boolean spelling follow `set_print_format`.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when rendering fails.

## `src/types/closure_custom.rs`

The custom MLX closure domain: the custom-transform (VJP), custom-JVP, and custom-VMAP closure variants built from Rust callables through payload trampolines.

Every payload is a `RefCell` of the Rust callable boxed into C memory; the matching destructor reclaims it. Callback panics are caught at the FFI boundary, converted to typed failures, and parked thread-locally for the caller's status translation so nothing unwinds across the C ABI. The shared trampoline machinery lives in `crate::types::closures`.

### `MlxClosureCustom`

```rust
pub struct MlxClosureCustom
```

Owned MLX custom-transform (VJP) closure, released exactly once.

### `MlxClosureCustom::from_fn`

```rust
pub fn from_fn<F>(callback: F) -> Result<Self, MlxCError> where F: FnMut(&[MlxArray], &[MlxArray], &[MlxArray]) -> Result<Vec<MlxArray>, MlxCError> + 'static,
```

Builds an owned custom-transform closure from a Rust callable that receives inputs, outputs, and upstream gradients.

```rust
pub fn empty() -> Self
```

Creates an empty custom-transform closure handle.


Copies the source closure handle into this handle.


Applies the custom transform.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when application fails.

## `src/types/closures.rs`

The MLX closure domain: owned closures built from Rust callables through payload trampolines, plus the kwargs and value-and-gradient variants. The custom-transform family lives in `crate::types::closure_custom` and shares this module's trampoline machinery.

Every payload is a `RefCell` of the Rust callable boxed into C memory; the matching destructor reclaims it. Callback panics are caught at the FFI boundary, converted to typed failures, and parked thread-locally for the caller's status translation so nothing unwinds across the C ABI.
